items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And then one day Herlin Riley, you know him? [INTERVIEWER] Yes.

ctx.x: What was the entrance into the music field that kind of cemented your — okay I’m going to do this — or was there one?

Well when I was about — just before I started playing with Papa French, I was about 19, and I went on Bourbon Street and I heard some of those guys play, and I wasn’t really impressed. So I was thinking I could actually play as well as this guy, you know, with a © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

little time under my belt. So that was very inspiring that this guy had a job and I could actually do that. So then I knew I could do it, I was a business major majoring in distributive education, DE. And in DE you had to have a job, because it’s like a management course. So I had a little job at Sears. So I was going to school full time, I was working at Sears plus playing a few little rock gigs here and there, and this guy used to come in and buy fishing equipment. I had no idea who he was. And then one day…
